narrative:
The model predicts you have a 35% chance of failing your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses to strengthen your preparation.

The prediction is driven mainly by three key aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is the reason you chose this school—reputation. Most students who passed selected the school for its academic course offerings, whereas your choice based on reputation worked against you in the model’s eyes and pulled the prediction toward failure.

The second most important factor is your history of one past class failure. Students who ultimately passed had zero previous failures on average, so this stands out as a clear warning sign that increased the model’s estimate of your risk.

Third, your low amount of free time after school also mattered. While this actually pushed the prediction slightly toward passing—perhaps because limited free time can sometimes reflect a more focused routine—it was not enough to outweigh the two stronger factors working against you.

To improve, you should focus on preventing any further setbacks by creating a structured weekly study plan that exceeds two hours, seeking extra academic support even if it isn’t currently offered, and reflecting on whether your current school environment truly matches your learning needs. Taking these steps now can meaningfully lower your risk before the final exams.
